parts.note: something harmful is bad for you
one's later years are old age

explanation.surface: Someone is warned that a husk-like waste will harm them as they grow old.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaff as a noun is light teasing banter, which is exactly what this word for playful repartee means.

clue.text: Does one have hard lines writing such poetry?

definitions.text: Does one have hard lines writing such poetry?

parts.words: Does one have hard lines writing such poetry?
parts.note: a style of verse whose lines are laid out as a shape on the page shares its name with the hard building material, so its poet works in 'hard lines'

explanation.surface: A rueful question about whether a certain kind of poet has a tough time of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaped or visual verse, where typography forms a picture, is called by this name, which also means a hard building material.

parts.note: a trophy is a prize such as a cup

explanation.surface: Someone thinks handing out a prize is a waste of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Wasting away of a muscle or organ is the medical sense of this noun.

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters of binges running out of control into a new order

explanation.surface: Folk are found at riotous drinking sessions.
explanation.definitionFit: Beings are living creatures, here human ones, so the plural noun stands for people.

clue.text: New air hostess turned out to give quality in the main

indicators.note: turned out suggests the three words being turned inside out and rearranged

explanation.surface: A newly hired flight attendant proves to be good at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' looks like an adjective for the hostess but is part of the fodder. 'The main' is a poetic word for the sea, so quality in the main is fitness for sea travel.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is a literary word for the open sea, and this noun is a ship's fitness to sail it.

parts.note: hunting for something is searching for it
a warrant is an official licence or authorisation

explanation.surface: A question about whether a policeman needs a permit to go hunting.
explanation.walkthrough: A bobby is British slang for a police officer; the whole clue describes the document that licenses a police officer's hunt through premises.
explanation.definitionFit: A court document authorising police to look through a property is exactly a licence for the bobby's hunt.

clue.text: Margaret Jones is falling for a soldier

indicators.note: falling suggests the letters of the name tumbling into disorder

explanation.surface: A woman named Margaret Jones is becoming infatuated with a military man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Falling for' reads as falling in love, but 'falling' alone signals the anagram of all thirteen letters of MARGARET JONES.
explanation.definitionFit: This senior non-commissioned rank is held by a soldier, so the title fits by example.

indicators.note: from tells us the letters are taken out of the words Tasmania cheering

explanation.surface: A supporter is heard roaring encouragement from Tasmania.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanatical enthusiast can be called this, an informal word for a wild devotee.

clue.text: Rainy condition on ring-road is common

parts.note: a ring is round, the shape of the letter O

indicators.note: condition suggests the word rainy being put into a different state

explanation.surface: Wet weather on the ring road is nothing unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'ring-road' is split in two: ring and road give separate pieces, while 'condition', read as weather, signals the anagram making INARY.
explanation.definitionFit: Common and this adjective are synonyms meaning usual or unremarkable.

indicators.note: comeback signals the word for standard coming back, read in reverse

parts.note: par is the standard, as in up to par

explanation.surface: A stinging retort is a typical reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comeback' looks like a retort, fitting the surface, but it turns PAR round.
explanation.definitionFit: A rap on the knuckles is a sharp reprimand, so the noun means a sharp rebuke.

definitions.meaning: to graze, as you might your knee in a fall
a pickle is an awkward predicament or fix

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to graze skin away; the noun is an awkward fix, like a pickle.

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so these are people who drive cattle, not tidy motorists

explanation.definitionFit: Neat is an archaic term for cattle, and these men drive or tend herds of them.

clue.text: Couple almost expected to acquire ring?

indicators.note: almost means the word for expected loses its final letter

parts.note: something expected is due
a ring is round, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: A pair are nearly due to buy a wedding ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acquire ring' suggests an engagement in the surface, but 'to acquire' only joins the pieces; 'almost' drops the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple and this word both mean a pair, especially of performers.

definitions.meaning: a defender who plays behind the back line
a crossing ... was a person kept busy clearing a street crossing

explanation.surface: A soccer player is occupied at a pedestrian crossing.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the defensive football position and the old street-crossing cleaner go by this name.

clue.text: Large sum of money for tea?

definitions.meaning: ... of money means a large amount
a vessel for brewing tea, the teapot

explanation.definitionFit: A pot can be a large sum, as in a jackpot, and also the vessel tea is brewed in.

indicators.note: after places the word for call behind the a and party

parts.note: a do is an informal party
to ring someone is to call them on the phone

explanation.surface: A fond telephone call is made after a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoring and loving are synonymous adjectives describing deep affection.

parts.note: a game played on top of a table, with tiles whose halves are matched end to end; it sounds like a league leader in football

explanation.definitionFit: Tiles divided into two halves, each with pips, are matched end to end in this tabletop game.

clue.text: Verdi composition would note and share again

indicators.note: composition suggests the letters of Verdi being composed anew

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I would, so would stands for these two letters
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: An opera by Verdi would add a note and be divided up once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition' looks musical, given Verdi, but it is the anagram signal: VERDI becomes REDIV, followed by ID and E.
explanation.definitionFit: To divide again is to share out once more, the meaning of the re- prefix plus divide.

clue.text: Percussion instrument least used at church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: used suggests the word least being worked over into a new form

explanation.surface: A percussion instrument is played least often in church services.
explanation.walkthrough: 'least used' reads as 'played least often', but 'used' is the anagram signal, turning the fodder into LESTA; CE, the Church of England, comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A keyboard instrument striking metal plates is classed with the orchestral percussion section.

clue.text: Facade beginning to take a long time

parts.note: the beginning of something is its front
an age is a long time

explanation.surface: Building a frontage takes forever to get started.
explanation.definitionFit: A facade is the front face of a building, which is what this noun names.

indicators.note: after places the word for quarrel behind the letter for midday

parts.note: N is noon, midday
a quarrel is a crossbow bolt, a kind of arrow

explanation.surface: An argument held after lunchtime is restricted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarrel' means an argument on the surface but here is a crossbow bolt.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrow and limited are synonyms, as in a narrow or limited outlook.

definitions.meaning: to grant or allot something to someone
to delegate a task to a person

explanation.definitionFit: This verb means both to allot something and to delegate a task to someone.

clue.text: Continental woman writes a note about Adam

indicators.note: about means the note goes around the name Adam

parts.note: me (or mi) is a note in the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A European lady pens a memo concerning a man named Adam.
explanation.definitionFit: Madame is the French form of address for a married woman, so a woman from the Continent.

indicators.note: sported by means worn by the word Leicestershire, which carries the letters; openers points to its start

explanation.surface: A flower necklace is worn by the opening batsmen of the county cricket team.
explanation.walkthrough: Openers are the first batsmen in cricket; here they point to the opening letters of Leicestershire, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hawaiian lei is a garland of flowers worn round the neck.

clue.text: A burden in the French game

indicators.note: in places a and the word for burden within the French article

parts.note: le is French for the
a cross to bear is a burden

explanation.surface: A heavy load weighs on the French.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacrosse is a field game played with netted sticks, an example of a game.

indicators.note: surprisingly hints that on Java turns up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: Someone is startled to find an indigenous American on an Indonesian island.
explanation.definitionFit: The Navajo are a Native American people of the south-western United States.

clue.text: Believed university lecturer to be a telepathist

parts.note: to have thought something is to have believed it
a reader is a senior university lecturer in Britain

explanation.surface: A lecturer was thought to be a mind reader.
explanation.walkthrough: In British universities a reader ranks just below a professor.
explanation.definitionFit: A telepathist claims to read minds, which this hyphenated noun describes.
